title: Sequencing, cloning, and antigen binding analysis of monoclonal antibodies isolated from single mouse B cells
protocol: Dilute antigen in PBS at the chosen concentration and mix with Alum at a 2:1 ratio.
Rotate the mixture at 4°C for 45 minutes.
Inject adjuvanted antigen into the footpad of anesthetized mice using an insulin syringe.
Dissolve tamoxifen in corn oil at 60 mg/ml.
Incubate the solution in a rotator at 60°C for at least 15 minutes.
Administer the tamoxifen solution via oral gavage with a plastic feeding tube and syringe.
Secure the mice with the knee down to expose the popliteal fossa.
Carefully separate the lymph node from surrounding adipose tissues and muscles using micro-dissecting tweezers and forceps.
Place the lymph node in a 70-μm polystyrene sterile cell strainer immersed in FACS Buffer (PBS 1× pH 7.2, 10% FBS, 2 mM EDTA) on ice.
Disaggregate the lymph node with the help of a 3 mL syringe plunger.
Filter the cell suspensions into a 15 mL conical tube using a new 70-μm polystyrene sterile cell strainer.
Bring the final volume to 10 mL with cold FACS Buffer.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of ACK Lysis Buffer and incubate for 1 min at 4°C to lyse red blood cells.
Stop the reaction by adding 10 mL of FACS Buffer.
Centrifuge the cells at 350 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 500 μL of FACS Buffer and transfer them to a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube.
Add anti-mouse CD16/32 to block Fc receptors (final concentration at 1 μg/mL) in FACS Buffer for 15 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge the tubes at 350 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Add fluorescently labeled antibodies and Dead Cells Marker (DCM) in PBS 1× pH 7.2, 2 mM EDTA without FBS.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of FB.
Centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 500 μL of FB.
Protect from light and keep at 4°C.
Sort single B cells into individual wells of a 96-well plate containing lysis buffer.
Add 5 μL of lysis buffer (TCL with 1% 2-β-mercaptoethanol) to each well of the 96-well PCR plate.
Seal the 96-well plate and place it on dry ice.
Bring RNA-SPRI beads to room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 30 min.
Mix RNA-SPRI beads thoroughly by vortexing.
Thaw the plate containing sorted B cells on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 × g for 30 s at 4°C.
Add 10 μL of nuclease-free water to each well.
Add 33 μL of RNA-SPRI beads per well and mix by pipetting.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 min.
Prepare wash buffer with 80% ethanol in nuclease-free water.
Place the plate on a DynaMag-96 side magnet.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature or until beads are attached to the tube wall next to the magnet.
Remove supernatant with a multichannel pipet without disturbing the bead pellet.
Add 125 μL of 80% ethanol to wash the beads.
Move the plate to an adjacent magnet column and let the beads move from side to side to ensure proper washing.
Carefully remove the ethanol.
Repeat the washes two more times with 80% ethanol for a total of 3 washes.
Air dry the bead pellets for 8–10 minutes.
Elute RNA from beads with 11 μL of reverse transcription (RT) Mix-1 per well.
Pipette up and down several times to resuspend the bead pellet.
Incubate the plates for 3 minutes at 65°C in a thermocycler.
Add 7 μL of RT Mix-2 per well.
Incubate the plate using the specified program in a thermocycler.
Add 10 μL/well of nuclease-free water to each well.
Proceed to immunoglobulin gene amplification by PCR or store the plate containing cDNA at −20°C or −80°C.
Resuspend lyophilized primers (50 μM) in RNase free water.
Prepare a working solution mix by mixing equal volumes of each primer.
Thaw the cDNA plate on ice.
Add 38 μL/well of PCR 1 mix in a new 96-well PCR plate.
Centrifuge the cDNA plate at 400 × g for 1 min at 4°C.
Transfer 3 μL of cDNA solution from the cDNA plate to the same position in the new 96-well plate containing PCR1 mix.
Place the plate in a thermocycler and incubate according to the specified program.
Proceed to the second step of amplification (PCR 2) or store the PCR1 plate at −20°C.
Resuspend lyophilized primers at 50 μM in RNase-free water.
Mix equal volumes of each primer to prepare a working solution mix.
Thaw the PCR 1 plate for 5 minutes on ice.
Prepare PCR mixes for the second step of PCR amplification (PCR 2) of IgH and IgK genes.
Centrifuge the PCR 1 plate at 400 × g for 1 minute at 4°C.
Transfer 4 μL of PCR 1 from each well to the same position in the PCR 2 plate.
Place the plate in a thermocycler and incubate according to the specified program.
Run 5 μL of the product of PCR 2 on a 2% agarose gel.
Sequence the PCR 2 products using the reverse primer of PCR 2.
Amplify heavy- and light-chain genes for cloning to add sequences homologous to the plasmid’s site of insertion.
Prepare a working solution mix by mixing equal volumes of each primer.
Thaw the first PCR plate for 5 minutes on ice.
Perform separate PCR reactions for variable heavy and light chain genes.
Prepare PCR mix for the cloning PCR for each chain.
Add 38 μL/well of cloning PCR mix in a new 96-well PCR plate.
Centrifuge the PCR 1 plate at 400 × g for 1 min at 4°C.
Add 4 μL of PCR 1 from each well to the same position in the Cloning PCR plate.

Place the plate in a thermocycler and run the following program: (Details of the specific steps in this program are not provided, so further specifics cannot be added here without additional information.)
Load 5 μL of the cloning PCR product from each well in a 2% agarose gel.
Run the gel at 140 V for 20 min.
Enzymatically digest plasmid containing the IgG constant region with AgeI and SalI.
Incubate at 37°C overnight (12–16 hours).
Add 1 μL of Alkaline phosphatase, calf intestinal (CIP) to de-phosphorylate the linearized vector.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Purify the linearized plasmid.
Run the digestion mix in a 1% agarose gel.
Cut the corresponding DNA band under UV light and purify using NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean-up system according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Purify the products of the cloning PCR using QIAquick 96 PCR Purification Kit or equivalent method based on sample number.
Sequence and Ligation-Independent Cloning (SLIC).
Prepare ligation mix on ice.
Mix 8.5 μL of ligation mix with 1/10 of the final volume of purified PCR product on ice.
Incubate the plates for 2.5 min at 25°C in a thermocycler.
Place the plate on ice for at least 10 min to stop the reaction.
Thaw chemically competent DH5α cells on ice.
Pipette 30 μL of competent cells into individual wells of a new 96-well plate.
While on ice, add 4 μL of the ligation reaction to the competent cells.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Heat shock the bacteria at 42°C for 40 s in a thermocycler.
Transfer the plate to ice and incubate for at least 1 min.
Add 40 μL of LB medium.
Place the plate on a shaker at a 45° angle and incubate at 210 rpm and 37°C for 40 min.
Streak transformed cells on prewarmed LB-antibiotic agar plates.
Incubate LB-antibiotic agar plates overnight at 37°C.
Reconstitute lyophilized primers at 50 μM in RNase-free water.
Mix equal volumes of each primer to prepare a working solution mix.
Screen bacterial colonies by PCR using the 5′ Ab sense forward primer and corresponding IgH or IgK reverse primers from PCR 2.
Add 25 μL of colony PCR mix per well in a new 96-well PCR plate.
Pick individual bacterial colonies with sterile pipette tips and introduce tips into individual wells containing the colony PCR mix.
Leave the tips inside the PCR mix until the next step.
Prepare a bacterial stock for each reaction by streaking each tip from the colony PCR plate on an LB-antibiotic agar plate.
Incubate LB-antibiotic agar plates at 37°C overnight (12–16 hours).
Load 5 μL of Colony PCR product from each well into a 2% agarose gel.
Run the gel at 140 V for 20 minutes.
Grow individual bacterial cultures carrying the heavy and light chain plasmids in LB media with antibiotic at 37°C and 220 rpm overnight (12–16 h).
Purify plasmid DNA from the bacteria cultures using a preferred commercial DNA isolation system.
Transfect HEK293-6E cells under a laminar flow hood.
Grow HEK293-6E cell cultures in suspension in FreeStyle 293 expression medium supplemented with penicillin and streptomycin.
Mix 25 μg of heavy chain DNA with 25 μg of light chain DNA or alternatively use 50 μg of pre-combined heavy and light chain DNA.
Bring the mixture to a total volume of 2.3 mL with PBS 1×.
Vortex the solution thoroughly.
Add 170 μL of 0.045% (wt/vol) polyethylenimine (PEI, 0.34% of cell culture volume).
Vortex the mixture for at least 15 seconds.
Add the DNA-PEI mixture to 50 mL of HEK293-6E cell culture.
Incubate the cells for 5–10 days at 130 rpm, 37°C, 95% humidity and 8.0% CO2.
Transfer the transfected HEK293-6E cell cultures to 50 mL tubes after incubation.
Centrifuge the tubes at 5,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.22 μm membrane filter to eliminate debris.
Purify Fabs by using Ni-beads according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
The Fab present in the culture supernatant are purified with Ni Sepharose beads because they are histidine-tagged.
Add 500 μL of Ni-beads to a poly-prep chromatography column.
Wash the column with 5 mL of distilled water.
Pass through 1 mL of 20 mM Imidazole buffer and let it go through by gravity.
Resuspend the beads with 500 μL of 20 mM Imidazole buffer in a new tube.
Mix 200 μL of beads with 50 mL of cell supernatant containing Fabs.
Incubate the mixture overnight (12–16 h) at 4°C in a spinning wheel.
Centrifuge the supernatants for 10 min at 300 × g and 4°C to pellet the beads.
Decant 2/3 of the supernatant carefully.
Pour the remaining supernatant containing the beads into the column.
Let it pass through by gravity.
Wash the column once with 1 mL of 20 mM Imidazole buffer.
Wash the column again once with 30 mM Imidazole buffer.
Elute in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes using 600 μL of 250 mM Imidazole buffer.
Perform buffer exchange with PBS 1× using 10K centrifugal filters according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Determine Fab productivity by measurement with nanodrop and PAGE analysis.
Store Fabs at 4°C for several years if required.
